ideaSummary:
Waste Ba – Turning Waste into Benefits

Waste Ba is a tech-enabled recycling startup that transforms waste into tangible community value while advancing the state’s ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) goals. By combining digital collection centers with a centralized waste processing and recycling facility, Waste Ba builds a scalable system that encourages responsible waste disposal, creates jobs, and promotes sustainable development.

At the core of the initiative is the “Waste Ba” token - a digital reward system that offers real, practical benefits to individuals who submit recyclable materials. These tokens can be converted to cash or used to access essential services such as healthcare, medication, and education-related fees (JAMB, WAEC, NECO). This turns ordinary waste into a tool for improving lives and livelihoods.

Our vision is to become a state-wide and ultimately, national model for smart recycling, where waste is not just disposed of but transformed into lasting value. With Waste Ba, every piece of waste is a step toward a cleaner environment, empowered citizens, and a more sustainable future.

Our mission is to create a cleaner, healthier, and more sustainable environment by building a digital, community-powered recycling system that transforms waste into economic and social value, empowering individuals, supporting essential services, and positioning our state as a model for ESG-driven development.

How Waste Ba Works:

1.	 Digital Collection Centers
Waste Ba will deploy a network of smart, tech-enabled collection hubs across the state, such as markets, schools, neighborhoods, and near major dumpsites. Residents can deposit sorted recyclables (plastic, paper, cans, glass) and receive Waste Ba tokens via a mobile app or USSD system.

This digital platform ensures real-time tracking, transparency, and scalability, empowering people from all socioeconomic backgrounds to participate easily.

2.	Central Recycling and Processing Facility
All collected materials are transported to a centralized recycling hub where they are cleaned, sorted, and processed into reusable raw materials. These products, which are shredded plastic or baled paper, are then sold to local manufacturers or exported to international markets that demand quality recycled inputs.

Strategic Focus on ESG & Infrastructure Development:
Waste Ba is not just a recycling platform; it is a long-term infrastructure investment that supports the state’s ambition to become ESG-compliant. By establishing modern recycling facilities, logistics systems, and data-driven operations, the startup contributes directly to:

a.	Environmental goals: This includes waste reduction, pollution control, and circular economy practices;
b.	Social impact: This contributes to community empowerment through rewards, job creation, and improved access to essential services; and
c.	Governance: This encourages transparency, accountability, and digital tracking of environmental metrics and community participation.

This positions Waste Ba as a key partner for governments, donor agencies, and sustainability-focused investors.

Revenue Model:
Low-cost recyclable input sourced from communities

Value-added to the waste through recycling processing

Sales to domestic manufacturers and international recycling markets

Potential for public-private partnerships and ESG grants

Conclusion
Waste Ba is a smart, scalable solution that turns waste into value. By combining technology, community incentives, and recycling infrastructure, we’re creating cleaner environments, empowering people, and supporting essential services.
problemStatement:
In many parts of Nigeria, inculding  Edo State, improper waste management is a growing concern. Some streets, gutters, and public spaces are littered with plastics, cans, papers, and other recyclables that are often dumped or burned. This leads to blocked drainage systems, flooding, land degradation, polluted water sources, and increased health risks,especially in low-income communities.

Despite the environmental impact, most recyclable waste goes uncollected due to the absence of structured systems and public incentives. Waste is treated as a nuisance rather than a resource, and the lack of modern recycling infrastructure makes it difficult to recover value from it. At the same time, many individuals and families in Edo struggle to afford basic healthcare, education, and essential needs.

Waste Ba provides a smart solution by turning waste into economic and social value. Through a digital reward system, people are encouraged to dispose of recyclables properly. The collected waste is then processed into reusable materials. This model not only promotes environmental cleanliness and a circular economy but also empowers underserved communities to access healthcare, pay school fees, and meet other needs—transforming waste into a tool for sustainable development in Edo State.

Nigeria generates an estimated 2.5 million tonnes of plastic waste annually, with Lagos alone contributing over 450,000 tonnes. A significant percentage of this waste ends up clogging drainage systems, polluting water bodies, and contributing to widespread flooding and disease outbreaks. Meanwhile, the youth in these areas struggle with joblessness, despite the increasing potential of the recycling economy.

The hub will collect, sort, and process plastic waste into reusable products such as paving tiles, flower pots, school chairs, and fence blocks. We are building a mobile-first on-demand and scheduled logistics platform that connects users with dispatch riders and delivery partners across various vehicle types—ranging from bicycles and motorcycles to trucks—based on their specific delivery needs. Think of it as the “Uber/Bolt” of logistics, but tailored for diverse use-cases beyond food delivery, such as groceries, furniture, school supplies, electronics, business packages, and more.

Unlike traditional courier systems that are rigid, expensive, and slow, our platform introduces intelligent, AI-assisted delivery scheduling, real-time tracking, and multi-vehicle logistics support. It also features voice-based order placement powered by AI, allowing users to speak naturally to place orders, schedule deliveries, or find nearby vendors.

We also embed a “minimart” module where vendors can showcase products. Business owners can manage deliveries seamlessly without building their own delivery infrastructure. Our approach includes onboarding students and local riders, thereby promoting job creation and inclusion.

We are currently targeting urban Nigerian markets, especially university communities and small business owners. With over 200 million people in Nigeria and logistics inefficiencies causing daily friction for consumers and SMEs, this platform aims to eliminate logistical barriers, improve last-mile delivery efficiency, and provide flexible income opportunities.

3. Unemployment among youth and students – We are onboarding students and unemployed youths as dispatch riders or micro-hub managers, creating opportunities for them to earn income flexibly.


4. Poor user experience in traditional logistics – Manual order placement, lack of tracking, and poor communication plague many courier services. We’re adding voice-assisted AI, smart scheduling, and real-time feedback for better UX.


5. Delayed adoption of AI in African tech – By embedding AI order processing and smart delivery suggestions, we bridge a tech gap and introduce innovation at scale

ideaSummary:
This comprehensive initiative aims to revolutionise the educational landscape in Edo State through a multifaceted approach targeting both educators and students. The core focus is on enhancing teaching methodologies, fostering a robust reading culture, and expanding educational access to underserved communities.

Firstly, we propose an intensive teacher training programme designed to bridge the gap between traditional pedagogical practices and modern, student-centred learning approaches. This programme will introduce educators to innovative teaching methods such as inquiry-based learning, flipped classrooms, and project-based learning. These methodologies aim to transform the classroom dynamic, positioning teachers as facilitators and students as active participants in their educational journey.

A pivotal aspect of this training will be the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into the educational framework. Teachers will be educated on the ethical and safe utilisation of AI in teaching and learning, with particular emphasis on effective prompt engineering for lesson planning and assessment development. This AI integration will be guided by the 80/20 principle, ensuring that educators maintain a strong foundational knowledge to effectively leverage AI tools.

The training will be delivered through a hybrid model, combining in-person workshops during school holidays with asynchronous virtual learning modules. This approach ensures maximum reach and flexibility, accommodating educators who may face constraints in attending physical sessions.

Secondly, we propose the establishment of reading clubs across schools in Edo State to cultivate a love for reading from an early age. This initiative will involve regular school visits to inaugurate these clubs, coupled with training for school heads on effective club management. A curated selection of physical books and e-books will be provided to support this endeavour.

The reading club initiative will extend beyond the school environment, incorporating a virtual component to ensure wider accessibility. Parents will be actively involved in this process, encouraging them to facilitate their children's engagement with educational content during leisure time. Age-appropriate materials, including picture books for younger children and vocabulary-building resources for older students, will be tailored to meet diverse learning needs.

Lastly, we aim to address the issue of educational access through a community outreach programme. This will involve visits to specific communities to engage with key stakeholders, including community leaders, parents, and rural dwellers. The objective is to raise awareness about the importance of education and to distribute physical copies of educational materials.

A critical focus of this outreach will be identifying out-of-school children and facilitating their enrolment in local schools. Follow-up mechanisms will be established to monitor attendance and progress, ensuring sustained engagement in the educational system.

This holistic approach aligns with Sustainable Development Goal 4, striving to provide quality education for all children in Edo State. By addressing teacher development, fostering a reading culture, and improving educational access, this initiative aims to create a ripple effect that will positively impact the educational outcomes of countless children across the state.

Through these innovative solutions, we aspire to transform the educational landscape of Edo State, equipping both educators and students with the knowledge necessary to thrive in the 21st century.
problemStatement:
This comprehensive initiative addresses several critical challenges facing the educational sector in Edo State. The primary issues tackled include:
1. Outdated Teaching Methodologies: Many educators in Edo State continue to rely on traditional, teacher-centred approaches that fail to engage students actively in the learning process. This solution addresses the need for modern, student-centred pedagogies that promote critical thinking, creativity, and active participation.

2. Lack of Continuous Professional Development: Teachers often lack access to ongoing training that would keep them abreast of contemporary educational practices and technologies. This initiative provides a platform for continuous learning and skill enhancement, bridging the gap between outdated training and current global standards.

3. Inadequate Integration of Technology: There is a significant deficiency in the use of modern technological tools, particularly artificial intelligence, in the educational system. This solution aims to equip teachers with the knowledge and skills to ethically and effectively integrate AI into their teaching practices.

4. Poor Reading Culture: Many students in Edo State struggle with reading fluency and comprehension, which impacts their overall academic performance. The proposed reading clubs address this by fostering a love for reading from an early age and providing access to age-appropriate reading materials.

5. Limited Educational Access: Certain communities, particularly in rural areas, face challenges in accessing quality education. This initiative extends beyond traditional classroom settings to reach underserved populations through community outreach and remote learning options.

6. Out-of-School Children: A significant number of children in Edo State are not enrolled in formal education. This programme aims to identify these children, facilitate their enrolment, and ensure their regular attendance through follow-up mechanisms.

7. Parental Engagement: There is often a disconnect between schools and parents, particularly in supporting children's educational journey. This solution actively involves parents in the reading club initiative and community outreach programmes, fostering a more holistic approach to education.

8. Digital Divide: Many students lack access to digital learning resources. By providing e-books and virtual learning opportunities, this initiative aims to bridge this digital gap and offer alternative educational pathways.

9. Contextual Learning Materials: There is a scarcity of learning resources that reflect the local context and experiences of Edo State children. This solution addresses this by providing materials that are relevant and relatable to the target audience.

By addressing these multifaceted challenges, the proposed solution aims to significantly enhance the quality of education in Edo State, aligning with Sustainable Development Goal 4 to provide inclusive and quality education for all. It seeks to create a ripple effect, where improvements in teacher training and student engagement lead to broader societal benefits and a more educated, skilled workforce for the future of Edo State.

ideaSummary:
Homiq is a trusted real estate web platform designed to connect individuals and businesses seeking to buy, rent, or lease properties (homes, land, commercial real estate) with pre-verified, professional real estate agents. Our goal is to eliminate fraud, ease the home search process, and offer a more transparent real estate experience for Nigerians — and eventually, the wider African market.

In Nigeria, real estate transactions are plagued by scams, impersonations, fake property listings, and unlicensed agents. People looking to rent or buy homes are forced to rely on word of mouth or unregulated online classified platforms like Jiji, where anyone can list properties — fake or real. This has led to countless cases of financial loss, identity theft, and even physical danger. Homiq solves this by curating a secure, tech-enabled marketplace where only vetted agents with traceable records are allowed to list properties.

Our model is simple yet powerful: Homiq works like a “Shopify for Real Estate”, allowing verified agents to open a mini-storefront for their properties. We offer tools like digital property portfolios, customer messaging, document upload features, and map-based search, all wrapped in a clean, mobile-first design.

We also plan to offer add-ons such as:

Legal advisory support on land/property purchases,

Property verification services for title deeds,

Ratings and reviews for agents,

Localized property search filters (e.g., distance to bus stop, water access, road type, etc.).


This project is starting in Nigeria, but has long-term scalability across African cities where urban housing demand is exploding and trustworthy digital platforms are lacking. Homiq will be Africa’s most trusted home marketplace — building trust, one home at a time.
problemStatement:
Homiq is built to address four major challenges in the Nigerian (and African) real estate industry:

1. Fraud and Scam Listings: Many platforms allow anyone to post listings, leading to impersonation, fake listings, and fraud. Homiq only allows verified agents with credentials and proof of past deals.


2. Lack of Trust: There’s no central, reliable system where users can compare agents, verify property titles, or confirm authenticity. Homiq solves this with transparency, ratings, and legal verification tools.


3. Poor Digital Experience: Traditional agencies are outdated, and most platforms are hard to navigate, lack filtering, and don’t provide updated listings. Homiq is modern, mobile-first, and tailored to the local context.


4. Inefficiency and Delay: The property search process is fragmented. Homiq centralizes listings, automates agent-buyer matching, and streamlines communication.

ideaSummary:

1.) Academic Tutorials & Mentor Matching:

In addition, we host mentorship sessions with best graduating students from top institutions, helping learners build confidence and gain practical study strategies to excel in school.


2.) Expert AI-Powered Career Advisor:
 Many students graduate from university with no clear career direction. As a result, they often waste time and energy pursuing jobs that don’t match their strengths or interests. Our AI-Powered Career Advisor solves this by asking users a few targeted questions and using real labor-market data to recommend careers that align with their interests and abilities. It also outlines the skills required for each path and the steps to take to get there.

4.) Built-In Opportunity Hub:
 To make sure learning leads to action, our platform includes a curated hub with up-to-date listings for internships, entry-level jobs, and scholarship opportunities. This ensures students can move directly from learning to earning.


To demonstrate our seriousness and belief in the vision, we have officially registered StudyBoosta Technologies with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) and enrolled with the Edo State Revenue Board for tax purposes. We’ve also built a pre-launch waitlist of over 1,000 eager learners who are ready to start learning as soon as we launch.
With over 9 million tertiary students facing learning disruptions across Africa, more than 36 million unemployed youth, and 85% of Nigerian graduates lacking essential digital skills, StudyBoosta is uniquely positioned to bridge the gap between learning, career clarity, and employability thereby empowering African youth to thrive academically, choose the right career path, and step confidently into high-income roles or entrepreneurship.

ideaSummary:
In today’s challenging economic realities, I strongly believe that it is no longer optional but absolutely necessary for every citizen to strive hard to remain financially relevant.

With rising unemployment and limited traditional job opportunities, I have chosen to think outside the box and pursue innovative means to secure my financial future and contribute meaningfully to the society.

One such venture that I am passionate about is small-scale catfish farming, using a tarpaulin mobile pond system. A practical, sustainable, and highly rewarding agribusiness model.

I will leverage on a corner piece of land beside my family house measuring about 35ft x 50ft and an already functional borehole water system, I intend to strategically set out to install a tarpaulin mobile fish pond measuring 18ft x 10ft x 4ft. This setup allows me to convert unused space into a thriving business hub, with minimal overhead costs and great potential for scalability.

Here’s how I intend to run this venture:
Setting Up the Pond: As an experienced catfish farmer, with well over 10 years of experience who has managed catfish farms for individuals in Benin City, Port Harcourt, and its environs. I will deploy a mobile tarpaulin pond that is easy to install and maintain. The size I have chosen supports an optimal stocking of up to 1,000 juvenile catfish, ensuring both profitability and ease of management.

Water Management: Thanks to my reliable borehole water supply, I can maintain excellent water quality, critical for healthy fish growth. I will implement a consistent filtration and water renewal schedule to enhance oxygen levels and overall fish health.

This gap leads to frustration, brain drain, reliance on informal or unstable jobs, and in many cases, pushes youth toward irregular migration in search of better prospects.

In rural and semi-urban areas of Edo, there’s an even wider digital divide. Many young people have smartphones but do not know how to use them as tools for income generation. Meanwhile, the global demand for remote workers continues to grow — but Edo youth are being left behind due to lack of exposure, training, and structured support.

As someone who migrated to the UK for work and built digital skills through self-effort, I understand the gap intimately. ideaSummary:
Mamcare is a new, easy-to-use digital service designed to support pregnant mothers in Nigeria, starting with Edo State. Think of it as having a caring health expert right in your pocket. Our goal is to give every mom important, accurate health information and support quickly, helping both her and her baby stay healthy. We aim to reach anyone, even those in the most remote locations, irrespective of their economic status or ability to own a smartphone.

Mamcare SMS: Simple Help for Everyone
Even if you have a very basic mobile phone, Mamcare has you covered with simple text messages.

- Weekly Pregnancy Updates: Once you sign up, we'll send you a text every week. These messages are tailored to your pregnancy stage. They'll tell you:
- What's happening with your baby's growth.
- Changes you might feel in your body and how to manage them.
- Tips for healthy eating and safe exercises.
- Important warning signs that mean you need to see a doctor quickly.
- Appointment Reminders: We'll send you texts to remind you about your clinic visits, so you don't miss important check-ups.
- Emergency Contacts: In an emergency, a quick text can get you numbers for ambulances or nearby health centers, along with basic first aid tips.
- After Baby Arrives: After delivery, we'll send tips for your recovery and reminders for your baby's immunizations.

Mamcare App: More Support on Your Smartphone
If you have a smartphone, the Mamcare app offers even more detailed help.

- Your Pregnancy Journey at a Glance: See your pregnancy progress with pictures and track how many weeks you have left.
- Complete Health Library: Find easy-to-understand articles, short videos, and audio clips on all pregnancy topics – from preparing for labor to breastfeeding and caring for your newborn.
- Symptom Checker: If you have a health worry, type in your symptoms. The app will give you simple advice on whether it's normal, needs watching, or if you should visit a doctor.
- Your Health Records: Keep your personal health details like weight and blood pressure safely in the app. You can even share them with your doctor.
- Book Clinic Visits: Easily find and book your doctor's appointments directly through the app.
- Find Nearby Clinics: Use your phone's map to find the closest hospitals and pharmacies when you need them.
- Connect with Other Moms: Join a safe chat group to talk with other pregnant mothers, share stories, and get support.
- Chat with Health Experts: During certain times, you can even text chat with a qualified nurse or midwife for personalized advice.
- Learn and Play: Enjoy fun quizzes to learn more about pregnancy and set reminders for your medicines or healthy habits.

Why Mamcare is Important
Mamcare is all about making healthcare easier and more accessible for pregnant women. By giving mothers reliable health information through both simple texts and a smart app, we help them make good choices for their health and their baby's health. This means healthier moms and healthier babies across Nigeria.
problemStatement:
Mamcare is designed to tackle several critical challenges that pregnant mothers in Nigeria, especially in Edo State, currently face:

- Limited Access to Reliable Health Information: Many pregnant women, particularly those in rural or underserved areas, lack easy access to accurate and timely health information about their pregnancy, fetal development, nutrition, and warning signs. This often leads to reliance on unreliable sources or traditional beliefs that may not be evidence-based.
- Missed Antenatal Appointments: A significant number of mothers miss crucial antenatal care visits due to forgetfulness, lack of awareness of appointment dates, transportation issues, or simply not understanding the importance of regular check-ups. This can delay the detection and management of potential complications.
- Geographic Barriers to Healthcare: For many, the nearest healthcare facility might be far away, difficult to reach due to poor road networks, or expensive to get to. This makes regular in-person consultations challenging and limits access to timely medical advice, especially in emergencies.
- Information Overload and Misinformation: In the digital age, while information is abundant, distinguishing reliable health advice from misinformation can be difficult and overwhelming for expectant mothers.
- Lack of Continuous Support and Monitoring: Beyond scheduled appointments, many mothers lack a consistent source of support or a way to monitor their health and their baby's development in between visits. This can lead to anxiety and delayed action when new symptoms arise.
- Poor Health Outcomes: These challenges collectively contribute to higher rates of maternal and infant mortality and morbidity, preventable complications during pregnancy and childbirth, and generally poorer health outcomes for both mothers and their newborns.

Mamcare directly addresses these problems by providing an accessible, reliable, and continuous digital healthcare companion, empowering mothers with knowledge and support, ultimately contributing to safer pregnancies and healthier babies.

Think of it as your one-stop shop for quick bites and refreshing sips! You can browse menus from different vendors, pick exactly what you want, and have it delivered quickly to your home or office. It's the perfect solution for satisfying those cravings or grabbing a light meal on the go.

Affordable, Eco-Friendly Delivery
A core part of PEEJ Snacks' plan is to use electric bicycles for all deliveries. This keeps our operational costs significantly lower than traditional delivery methods, allowing us to offer really cheap delivery to everyone. Plus, it's a win for the environment, helping to reduce pollution in Benin City.

Empowering Youth and Local Businesses
By using electric bikes, PEEJ Snacks will create many job opportunities for young people as delivery riders. We'll provide them with training, fair wages, and a supportive work environment, helping them gain valuable experience. We're also eager to partner with local pastry chefs, caterers, and drink makers, giving them a platform to reach more customers without the need for their own delivery setup. This approach truly fosters entrepreneurship and culinary talent within Benin City.

Agriculture remains the backbone of many developing economies, providing employment, food, and income for a large portion of the population. However, global food systems are under increasing pressure due to population growth, climate change, urbanization, and declining natural resources. To achieve food security - defined as access to sufficient, safe, and nutritious food - innovation across the agricultural value chain is essential.

Innovation in Farming

Farming is the starting point of the food system, and innovation here can significantly boost productivity and resilience. Traditional farming methods often result in low yields, heavy labor, and vulnerability to weather fluctuations. Modern solutions such as precision agriculture use technologies like GPS, drones, and data analytics to help farmers monitor soil health, track crop growth, and apply inputs efficiently.

Improved seed varieties developed through research - such as drought-tolerant, pest-resistant, and fast-growing crops—are vital for adapting to changing climates. Innovations like hydroponics, aquaponics, and vertical farming allow food production in non-traditional environments, reducing land use and conserving water. Mobile-based advisory services also support smallholder farmers with weather updates, planting guides, and market information.

Innovation in Food Production

After farming, the next critical phase is food processing and production. In many regions, a significant amount of food is lost post-harvest due to poor handling, lack of processing infrastructure, and inadequate storage. Innovations such as solar dryers, airtight silos, and small-scale food processors help reduce post-harvest losses and add value to raw produce.

The rise of alternative proteins—such as plant-based meat, lab-grown meat, and edible insects—offers sustainable solutions to meet protein demand while reducing the environmental impact of livestock farming. In addition, advancements in biotechnology and food fortification are helping to address malnutrition by improving the nutrient content of staple foods.

Innovation in Distribution

A well-functioning distribution system ensures that food moves efficiently from farm to consumer. In many developing regions, inadequate transport infrastructure and storage facilities result in high food waste and increased prices. Innovations such as cold chain logistics, mobile-based supply chain platforms, and e-commerce marketplaces are improving access to food and reducing losses.

Blockchain and traceability technologies are also gaining traction, enabling greater transparency and safety across food supply chains. Digital platforms that connect farmers directly with buyers are cutting out intermediaries and increasing farmers' profits while offering consumers lower prices and fresher products.

Conclusion

Innovation in agriculture and food systems is not just about technology—it is about rethinking how food is grown, processed, and distributed to meet the needs of a growing and changing world. These innovations offer promising solutions to long-standing challenges, but their success depends on supportive policies, investment in infrastructure, and inclusive access for smallholder farmers and rural communities.

Empowering local stakeholders, strengthening education and training, and fostering collaboration between governments, the private sector, and research institutions are essential to building sustainable, resilient, and equitable food systems for the future.
problemStatement:
The Problem: Food Insecurity and Inefficiency in Agricultural Systems

Many countries, especially in Africa and other developing regions, face chronic food insecurity—a situation where large parts of the population do not have regular access to sufficient, nutritious food. This is driven by a complex mix of challenges:

1. Low agricultural productivity

Most smallholder farmers use outdated tools and techniques, leading to poor yields.

Limited access to quality seeds, fertilizers, and knowledge restricts growth.



2. Climate change and environmental stress

Rising temperatures, droughts, and flooding reduce crop reliability.

Soil degradation and water scarcity worsen farming conditions.



3. Post-harvest losses and poor processing

A large percentage of harvested crops (sometimes up to 40%) are lost due to poor storage, handling, and lack of processing facilities.



4. Inefficient food distribution systems

Poor roads, lack of cold storage, and high transportation costs mean food often doesn’t reach markets on time or in good condition.

Middlemen often take a large share of profits, leaving farmers underpaid and consumers with high prices.



5. Poor market access and weak supply chains

Farmers in rural areas struggle to access buyers, finance, and reliable market information.

Lack of trust and transparency in supply chains leads to waste, inefficiency, and exploitation.



The Solution: Innovation in Farming, Production, and Distribution

This solution - integrating innovation across the food value chain - helps to solve the problem by:

1. Boosting productivity and resilience

Precision agriculture and improved seeds increase crop yields.

Mobile apps and advisory tools give farmers real-time guidance.

Climate-smart techniques help farms survive in changing weather conditions.

2. Reducing waste and improving food quality

Solar dryers, cold storage, and efficient processing reduce post-harvest losses.

Value-added processing increases shelf life and creates more diverse food products.

3. Improving market access and farmer incomes

Digital platforms connect farmers directly to buyers, reducing dependency on middlemen.

Transparent pricing systems and mobile payments ensure fairer compensation.

4. Strengthening food supply chains

Smart logistics and blockchain improve tracking, storage, and delivery of food products.

E-commerce and digital distribution expand market reach and reduce delays.

5. Making food more affordable and accessible

Efficient production and distribution lower the cost of food.

Nutritionally enhanced products help address malnutrition.

GreenCorridor Solutions 

GreenCorridor Solutions is an eco-impact business that operates on a waste-to-wealth model. We convert environmental trash such as tyres, sand, plastic waste, into useful, sellable, and installable products. These include painted tyre flower pots, tyre-based bioswales for drainage, and affordable eco-landscaping packages for schools, homes, markets, and religious centers. 

Our vision is to become the leading environmental beautification and flood-prevention service in Edo State,
driven by community impact, sustainability, and youth-led innovation.

In order to construct visually appealing, erosion-resistant corridors along streets, gutters, and public areas, the business gathers used tyres, repurposes them into flower pots and drainage reinforcements, and mixes them with natural plants like vetiver grass.

This is our straightforward yet effective value offer: we assist communities in finding cost-effective, appealing, and community-owned solutions to flooding, erosion and waste issues. In contrast to traditional drainage solutions which rely on expensive infrastructure, our eco-friendly approach uses local labour and waste materials to provide a more sustainable, engaging, and visually pleasing alternative. Clients benefit not only from functional improvements but from the beautification of their spaces, increased awareness of green practices, and the knowledge that their projects support youth empowerment and climate action.

One of our most innovative solutions is the creation of bioswales: shallow, green channels designed to manage stormwater runoff. These bioswales are built using repurposed tyres to line the edges, then filled with compost, gravel, and water-loving plants like vetiver and banana. The design naturally slows, filters, and absorbs rainwater, helping to prevent flooding, reduce erosion, and clean runoff before it enters waterways. Unlike cement gutters, bioswales are living systems that provide drainage and beauty, while being more cost-effective and environmentally friendly.

Our business generates income through two main channels: first, by selling recycled tyre products such as flower pots, tyre-bordered bioswales directly to individuals, event decorators and organizations; and second, by offering eco-beautification services to areas facing erosion or waste buildup. These services are sold as project packages and include all materials, design, installation, and optional maintenance. We plan to expand by offering hands-on training and certification programs to youths interested in launching their own GreenCorridor-style initiatives, growing our impact while creating new income streams.

ideaSummary:
In the heart of Benin City, a young mother named Osaro rushed her child to the hospital after a severe bout of food poisoning. The culprit? Contaminated meat purchased from a local open market. Sadly, this is not an isolated case. Across Edo State, families gamble with their health daily due to unsafe meat handling, poor hygiene, and lack of cold storage. That moment sparked a question in us: Shouldn’t access to safe, clean, and affordable meat be a basic right, not a privilege?

This is where Meatloaf Foods comes in — a homegrown solution reimagining how Edo feeds its people.

Our vision is to build a safe, smart, and sustainable meat ecosystem for Edo State — one that protects public health, supports local economies, and helps communities thrive.

We start by addressing the root problem: unhygienic slaughtering and poor meat distribution. Our solution introduces mobile hygienic meat processing units, training for local butchers, and the deployment of solar-powered cold rooms across local markets and communities. This helps reduce foodborne illness while preserving meat quality, especially in areas with unreliable electricity.

To make meat more affordable amid rising food prices, we created “MeatShare”, a digital platform that allows people to pool money and buy meat in bulk at wholesale prices. This group-buying model makes nutritious meat accessible to families who would otherwise be priced out, while also strengthening communal ties.

But we didn’t stop there. Every year, tons of animal waste in Edo markets are dumped into the environment, polluting water bodies and releasing harmful methane gases. This circular economy model creates green jobs and income, especially for women and youth in the meat value chain.

We also believe in the power of technology. Our “MyMeat Wallet” mobile app lets customers subscribe to monthly meat boxes, trace where their meat came from, and earn loyalty rewards. Whether you live in Uselu or Esan, Meatloaf Foods makes clean, traceable meat just a tap away.

By combining innovation, tradition, and sustainability, we are not just solving a problem — we’re setting a new standard. Our long-term goal is to build a Meat Innovation Hub in Edo, serving the entire South-South region with safe meat and eco-friendly byproducts.

At Meatloaf Foods, we believe Edo State can lead the way in food security, green innovation, and inclusive prosperity. It starts with meat — but ends with healthier homes, empowered communities, and a cleaner environment.

Because when we protect what our people eat, we protect our future.
problemStatement:
Our solution addresses three interconnected problems in Edo State’s meat sector:

Public Health Risks from Unsafe Meat:
A large portion of meat consumed in Edo is processed and sold under unhygienic conditions — often exposed to flies, dust, and heat in open markets without proper sanitation or cold storage. This leads to frequent foodborne illnesses, such as typhoid, cholera, and severe gastrointestinal infections, especially among children and the elderly.
Environmental Pollution from Livestock Waste:
Animal waste from abattoirs and meat markets is typically dumped in the open, clogging drainage systems and contaminating nearby water sources. The methane released from this untreated waste contributes to greenhouse gas emissions and climate change. This also deprives communities of potential value that could be recovered from the waste.
Food Insecurity and Rising Prices:
Due to inflation, middlemen exploitation, and inefficient distribution, meat has become unaffordable for many households. There is no system for collective purchasing or equitable access to safe, quality meat. At the same time, many small-scale meat vendors — particularly women and youth — struggle to earn sustainable income due to limited market access, poor infrastructure, and lack of training.
These problems are not just technical or economic — they affect the dignity, health, and resilience of Edo’s communities. By addressing them through innovation, sustainability, and inclusiveness, our solution reimagines a better future for food and livelihoods in the state.

problemStatement:
When I first started baking from my tiny kitchen, I noticed a problem that many families faced: finding truly fresh, high-quality cakes was harder than it should be. So many people would call me, often at the last minute, saying, “Promise, I need a cake today, but I want it fresh — not one that’s been sitting in a fridge for days.” It broke my heart to hear mothers worry about buying cakes packed with sugar that their children shouldn’t eat, or diabetic loved ones having to skip cake altogether.

I realised quickly that our community needed more than just a bakery — we needed a brand that would promise freshness every single day and healthier options that no one else offered. That’s how I started baking sugar-free cakes alongside our regular recipes, so every family could celebrate safely and joyfully.

But that wasn’t the only gap I saw. Many of my customers didn’t just want a cake — they wanted a surprise that would melt someone’s heart. I remember one young man who ordered a cake to surprise his mother on her birthday; when I delivered it with flowers and a handwritten note, the tears in her eyes reminded me why this business must be about creating memories, not just selling cakes. So I turned that into part of our brand: personalized surprise packages that turn ordinary days into unforgettable moments.

Yet the biggest problem that tugged at my heart was unemployment — especially for the youth and young women around me. Too many of them sat at home, bright and talented, but without practical skills or jobs to earn a living. That’s why I opened up my kitchen as a training space — to teach them how to bake, decorate, and build something for themselves. Many of my trainees have now started small baking businesses or help their families with extra income — and this gives me more joy than any cake I’ve ever baked.

Finally, as my little brand grew, I promised myself that success should never come at the cost of our environment. So I made choices to buy from local markets, bake to order (so nothing goes to waste), and pack our cakes in eco-friendly boxes that don’t litter our streets. I teach my students the same values: that being responsible bakers means protecting our community and planet too.

In the end, DUNAMIS CAKE AND MORE is my answer to four real problems I see daily:
✨ Families deserve fresh, healthier cakes.
✨ People deserve to surprise their loved ones with thoughtful gifts.
✨ Young people deserve skills and hope for a better tomorrow.
✨ And our environment deserves care from businesses like ours.

This is the heart behind every cake I bake — and the reason I believe this grant will help me do even more good, for even more people.

Rooted in the heart of Benin City, this business will revive and commercialize indigenous spice blends that have been passed down through generations, yet are gradually fading from current day kitchens. These include native seasonings like Oriema, Ikposa and other authentic spices unique to Bini cuisine.
The core mission of this business is cultural preservation through food. In every society, food is a key vessel of identity, storytelling, and heritage. By curating and packaging these spices, we are not only providing flavor-rich cooking solutions to households and restaurants, but also preserving the stories, names, and uses of ancestral ingredients that risk being forgotten. My business was created in response to an urgent cultural challenge: the steady erosion of Bini culinary traditions. Many of the indigenous spices and ingredients that once defined our meals and connected us to our heritage are disappearing from daily use. With younger generations growing up without the knowledge or experience of these flavors, we are witnessing a loss not just of food, but of identity, stories, and cultural continuity.

Another major issue is the lack of accessibility to these traditional spices in the market. Even when available, they are often unbranded, poorly processed, or stripped of their cultural value. This absence limits consumer choice and contributes to the discrimination against our local foods. 

My business is stepping in to fill this gap by professionally curating, packaging, and branding traditional Bini spices complete with the cultural stories, meanings, and recipes that bring them to life.

I am also addressing a pressing economic problem. Rural women and local farmers who are the custodians of these native spices operate mostly in informal, low-income markets. Despite their deep knowledge and labor, they often lack access to structured value chains and fair compensation. 

My business model ensures that these communities benefit meaningfully from their contributions.

Health is another critical issue. Traditional Bini spices are rich in nutrients and natural medicinal properties, but are increasingly being replaced by artificial seasonings and chemically processed flavorings. My products promote a return to wholesome, natural ingredients rooted in our heritage.

At its core, this business is a response to multiple interwoven problems—cultural loss, market failure, rural economic exclusion, and unhealthy food practices. 

My goal is to create a sustainable, culturally rich, and socially inclusive brand that not only revives ancestral flavors but also uplifts the people who preserve them. In doing so, we aim to bridge the gap between our past and our future through the power of food.

Imagine a learning platform that not only teaches but also transforms. A digital ecosystem that meets African students exactly where they are whether in school, at home, or out of school entirely, and equips them with the skills, mindset, and confidence to thrive in a future that’s already here.

We’re building a globally scalable, AI-powered EdTech platform, starting in Edo State, Nigeria, designed to bridge the significant gap between what schools teach and what life demands. This isn’t just about textbooks and tests. It’s about real-world readiness critical thinking, financial literacy, emotional intelligence, digital fluency, and the kind of creative confidence that turns ideas into innovation.
At its core, the platform offers personalized, bite-sized learning journeys, tailored by AI to match each learner’s pace, interests, and learning style. No more one-size-fits-all. This is education that adapts, evolves, and empowers.
But we don’t stop there.

We’re working on three powerful paths for engagement:
DIY (Do-It-Yourself) – For self-driven learners who thrive on autonomy, guided by gamified modules and smart learning paths.
DWY (Done-With-You) – A blend of mentorship, group learning, and tutor support for those who need a little guidance and community.
DFY (Done-For-You) – Structured homeschooling and micro-schooling options for parents seeking a personalized, high-touch experience.
Beyond students, we’re building a community of educators, facilitators, and curriculum designers, empowered to co-create and customize content. The platform becomes not just a tool but a movement, driven by collaboration and local relevance.

For parents and educators, intuitive dashboards offer live insights into student growth, habits, and gaps turning guesswork into strategy. Policymakers can finally make data-informed decisions with visibility into systemic performance like never before.
We begin with localized content and culturally resonant storytelling working hand-in-hand with schools, communities, and NGOs. A freemium model ensures accessibility for underserved learners, while premium services provide sustainability and scale.

But the dream doesn’t stop in Nigeria. Our vision expands across Africa and into other emerging markets creating the go-to infrastructure for future-focused education. A digital launchpad for self-aware, globally competent young people who think critically, act ethically and lead boldly.
This isn’t just an app. It’s a revolution in how we learn, grow, and build the future one learner at a time.
problemStatement:

In rural and underserved areas, quality education is a luxury. Power outages, poor infrastructure, and limited teacher access widen the gap. Many youths drop out, not because they can’t learn, but because the system forgets them.
Even those who stay are underprepared for the future. The curriculum is decades behind. Innovation, entrepreneurship, and tech readiness are missing. Teachers are overworked. Parents just want their children to succeed. Everyone is doing their best but the system is not prepared for what’s coming.

We’re here to reimagine it.
Our platform will deliver project-based, future-focused learning that builds critical skills not just grades. It will run on mobile, work offline, and offer DIY, DWY, and DFY learning models making it flexible, accessible, and scalable.
Dropouts will return. Teachers will be empowered. Parents will see. Policymakers will know. And learners will finally be ready for a world that’s already changed.

I felt helpless watching him go, knowing that help was out there but couldn't reach him fast enough. That terrible experience made me realize we needed a better way, and that's why I started building Crimson Care.

When someone is very sick or hurt and needs blood, getting the right type quickly can save their life. But today, finding blood is often hard and slow. Hospitals and blood banks don't always know what blood others have, and getting it delivered can take too long. This old way of doing things uses a lot of paperwork, has poor communication, and faces many roadblocks. When time is critical, these problems can be fatal.

Crimson Care is a new, smart solution that uses AI (Artificial Intelligence) to fix these problems. It's like a fast bridge that connects patients who need blood with the exact blood types available in hospitals and blood banks. Our AI helps us do this quickly and accurately.

The AI brain of Crimson Care instantly checks lots of information. It knows what blood type a patient needs, how much blood each hospital and blood bank has, and how close they are. When a patient needs blood, our system immediately looks at all available blood stock. This stops people from having to call around and saves a lot of time finding the right blood. The AI also picks the best match, looking at the closest blood, how urgent the patient's need is, and even guessing future blood needs to prevent shortages.

But Crimson Care doesn't just find the blood; it also helps get it there fast. Once we find a match, the system quickly arranges for special transport to deliver the blood safely to the patient. This makes delivery times shorter, keeps the blood fresh, and makes sure life-saving blood arrives when it's needed most. You can also track the blood unit as it travels, so doctors know exactly where it is.

Crimson Care will make a huge difference. By making the whole process faster and smoother, it will help save many lives in emergencies. Hospitals will know what blood is available nearby, helping them prepare better. Blood banks can manage their stock more efficiently and waste less blood. In short, Crimson Care is more than just a matching tool; it's a smart system that will change emergency healthcare by making sure no one loses their life because blood wasn't available or couldn't get to them in time.
problemStatement:
This solution addresses the critical problem of inefficient and delayed blood procurement and delivery in medical emergencies.

Specifically, it tackles:

1. Difficulty in real-time blood type matching: Hospitals struggle to quickly find compatible blood types due to fragmented inventory information across various facilities and blood banks.

2. ⁠Slow delivery of blood units: Manual processes, communication gaps, and logistical hurdles lead to significant delays in transporting life-saving blood to patients, especially for rare blood types or urgent needs.

3. Lack of centralized visibility: There's no unified system to show immediate blood availability across a region, leading to wasted time and potentially fatal outcomes.

4. Inefficient resource allocation: Hospitals and blood banks can't optimize their stock or respond effectively to emergencies without real-time data on supply and demand.

ideaSummary:
Pure Breed Farms is a startup agribusiness idea based in Benin City, Edo State, with a vision to produce affordable, high-quality animal feed for poultry, pig, and fish farmers across the state. The concept was born out of real conversations with smallholder farmers in Egor, Ikpoba-Okha, and Ovia North-East LGAs, who frequently complain about the poor quality and high cost of feed, which limits their production and profits.

The startup intends to set up a mini feed mill in Benin City that will process locally available raw materials like maize, cassava peels, palm kernel cake, rice bran, and groundnut cake into well-balanced feed formulas. These feeds will be specifically designed for livestock common in Edo State: broiler and layer chickens, catfish, and pigs. The goal is to improve animal performance, reduce mortality, and help farmers increase yield without the heavy burden of high-cost imported feed.

In addition to feed production, Pure Breed Farms will offer basic farmer support through training on feed handling, storage, and animal nutrition. The long-term goal is to strengthen food security in Edo State by supporting the livestock value chain and reducing dependence on external feed suppliers.
problemStatement:
Livestock farming is a key part of the economy in Edo State, especially in peri-urban and rural communities like Uselu, Ehor, Okada, and Abudu. However, farmers face three major problems:

High Cost of Feed: Many local poultry and pig farmers spend over 60% of their production costs on feed, which is often priced beyond their reach. With inflation and naira devaluation, imported feed components are becoming unaffordable.

Poor Quality Feed in Local Markets: Some farmers buy unlabelled or poorly formulated feed from open markets, especially at Oliha, New Benin, and Ekiosa, leading to poor animal growth, slow weight gain, and even death.

Lack of Local Alternatives: There are very few locally based feed producers in Benin City, and most rely on supplies from Lagos or the North. This creates delays, high transport costs, and inconsistent availability.

Pure Breed Farms aims to solve these problems by offering affordable, locally produced, and nutritionally sound feed, using raw materials sourced from within Edo and neighboring states. This will help stabilize prices, improve livestock health, and boost farmer productivity.

ideaSummary:
Dockintor.com is a healthcare innovation platform that will transform how people in Edo State access medical expertise. The goal is simple but powerful: to connect residents—especially in rural, underserved, and low-income communities—with licensed doctors and specialists through both digital and offline channels, including SMS and USSD services.
Edo State faces significant barriers to accessible and timely healthcare. In many LGAs, particularly in remote or riverine areas, residents must travel long distances to see a doctor, often without guaranteed access to a specialist. High consultation costs, widespread self-medication, and poor health literacy continue to worsen health outcomes across the state.
Dockintor.com aims to close this gap by allowing people to consult with doctors directly from their mobile phones. Whether it’s a pregnant woman in Esan West needing urgent guidance, a farmer in Ovia North-East worried about an infection, or a young adult in Benin City with questions about a chronic condition, Dockintor will bring expert care within reach—quickly, privately, and affordably.

Core Features Tailored for Edo State
Chat-Based Medical Consultations Residents with smartphones will access Dockintor.com to chat with verified doctors, ask questions, receive early diagnoses, and get digital referrals to appropriate healthcare facilities.
SMS & USSD Access for Low-Connectivity Areas To ensure no one is left out, residents in communities with poor internet—like Orhionmwon, Uhunmwonde, or Etsako Central—will be able to connect using SMS or USSD codes. They can request a doctor call-back, receive automated health tips, or schedule consultations using basic phones.
Community Health Integration Dockintor will partner with local health workers, NYSC members, and community leaders to promote the service, assist elderly and low-literacy users, and provide localized health education. These advocates will help build trust and ensure platform adoption across diverse communities.
Referral and Support Network For cases requiring physical examination or treatment, Dockintor will refer patients to the closest and most appropriate health facility within the state’s public or private system, streamlining access and reducing delays.

Transforming Healthcare Behavior and Access
Dockintor.com is more than just a digital service—it will be a vital tool in reshaping how Edo State residents seek, trust, and act on medical advice. By providing quick access to qualified professionals and supporting inclusive communication channels, Dockintor will promote early intervention, reduce preventable complications, and help build a healthier, better-informed population.
Through a mix of technology, community engagement, and culturally relevant communication, Dockintor.com will be a game-changer for health equity in Edo State.
problemStatement:
The Problem Dockintor.com Is Solving
Access to timely, professional, and affordable healthcare remains a major challenge in Edo State—especially for people living in rural communities, informal urban settlements, and low-income households. The core problems include:

1. Limited Access to Qualified Medical Professionals

Many residents in Edo State have little to no access to licensed doctors or specialists, particularly in remote LGAs and riverine areas. Most available care is provided by under-resourced primary healthcare centers or informal practitioners. For many, seeing a doctor requires long travel, high transport costs, and hours of waiting, discouraging them from seeking care at all.

2. Widespread Self-Medication and Health Misinformation

Due to cost, stigma, or inconvenience, people often turn to self-diagnosis, patent medicine vendors, or unverified online sources. This leads to frequent misuse of drugs, delayed treatment, complications, and in some cases, death from preventable conditions. There is a dangerous gap between symptoms and professional advice.

3. Digital Divide in Health Access

Even as telemedicine grows, most platforms require stable internet access, smartphones, and a certain level of digital literacy. This excludes large segments of the population—particularly the elderly, people in rural areas, and those with only basic mobile phones.

4. Overburdened Health Facilities

Hospitals and clinics in Edo State are often overwhelmed with cases—many of which could be triaged or resolved through basic health consultations. This contributes to poor patient experiences and delays in attending to urgent cases.

In Summary:
Dockintor.com is solving the problem of medical inaccessibility by:

Making healthcare affordable and accessible from anywhere in Edo State.
Providing trusted medical advice via chat, SMS, and USSD—with or without internet.
Reducing self-medication and misinformation by connecting people directly with verified doctors.
Supporting the healthcare system by offering first-contact, triage-level support that eases hospital congestion.
Empowering the public with timely, clear, and culturally relevant health information.

ideaSummary:
My Ideas to Transform Edo State
 
Edo State is a cultural powerhouse — home to the ancient Benin Kingdom, bronze artistry, and rich oral traditions. Yet today, much of its cultural heritage is under-promoted, under-preserved, and under-leveraged. These fine art ideas aim to change that by blending tradition, tourism, education, and economic opportunity.
  
1. Benin Heritage Murals
 
Large, hand-painted murals across various towns like Benin City, will depict Obas, warriors, and folktales. 
Impact: Beautifies the city, draws tourists, and educates the public about Edo history.
  
2. Community Sculpture Parks
 
Public parks and open spaces can be turned into cultural landmarks with bronze heads, masks, and symbolic figures. 
Impact: Promotes tourism, creates photo-worthy attractions, and brings history into daily life.
  
3. Hyperrealism Gallery: "Edo in portraits"
 
An art exhibition focused on charcoal and pencil portraits of real Edo people — market women, elders, students. 
Impact: Preserves modern-day Edo identity and gives local artists visibility. The gallery can travel across Nigeria and beyond.
  
4. Edo African Art Biennale
 
A bi-annual festival that gathers artists from across Africa and the diaspora in Benin City. Impact: Establishes Edo as a creative hub, boosts the local economy, attracts global attention, and creates a platform for local artists in Edo 
  
5. Art in Schools: Edo Future Creators
 
A program to teach schoolchildren painting, sculpture, and digital art tied to Edo heritage. Impact:Empowers youth, preserves culture, and builds creative careers from an early age
  
 Why This Matters:
 
These projects would:
 
- Boost cultural tourism
 
- Preserve Edo traditions visually
 
- Create platforms for local artists

- Inspire youth with identity and skills
 
- Position Edo as a modern African art destination
 

 
With the right partnerships and support, Edo can transform its streets, schools, and public spaces into living, breathing cultural experiences.
Let’s use art to tell our story — and invite the world to see it.
problemStatement:
Challenges of Art, Culture, and Tourism in Edo State 
  
1. Culture is Hidden, Not Celebrated Edo has amazing history — kings, warriors, bronzes — but most of it isn’t visible in everyday life. So what? People forget what they can’t see.
  
2. Tourists Aren’t Staying Edo should be a tourist magnet, but most visitors come and go quickly. **So what?** The state loses money and attention.
  
3. Artists Have Talent, But No Stage We have brilliant artists, but few places to show their work or get noticed. So what? Many give up or leave Edo to succeed.
  
4. Youth Are Out of Touch with Culture Young people know more about foreign trends than their own heritage. So what? Traditions fade, and pride disappears.
  
5. Our Stories Are Disappearing Too much culture is stuck in memory — not written down or shared online. So what? Once elders are gone, the stories could be lost forever.
  
6. Edo Is Not on the Global Map Ancient Edo art is famous, but modern Edo isn’t in big art shows or festivals. So what?We miss out on international recognition and funding.
  
7. Cultural Sites Are Worn Out or Forgotten Historic places aren’t being maintained or made interesting for visitors. So what? They get ignored instead of celebrated.
  
8. Events Happen, But No One Knows Great cultural events are poorly advertised and barely promoted. So what? People miss out, and the impact stays small.
  
The Big Picture
 
Edo has the stories, the talent, and the legacy — it just needs the spotlight. With better promotion, support, and creativity, the state can turn its heritage into a powerful cultural brand.

ideaSummary:
SkillBridge is an innovative, hybrid digital and community-based platform designed to tackle the growing challenge of youth unemployment in Edo State. The platform will connect unemployed and underemployed young people with skilled professionals (mentors) in high-demand sectors—such as technology, fashion, agriculture, health tech, media, solar energy, and construction—for hands-on training, project-based learning, and future job placement.
At its core, SkillBridge will operate on a “learn-by-doing + earn-while-learning” model. This approach will ensure that young people acquire practical, market-relevant skills while simultaneously gaining real-world work experience and earning income during the training period. We believe this will make skill development both empowering and economically meaningful.
How It Will Work
Mentees will create profiles and select their preferred career paths on the SkillBridge website. Skilled professionals and tradespeople (mentors) will also register, listing their areas of expertise, availability, and mentoring capacity. An AI-powered matching engine will connect mentors and mentees based on interests, location, and local economic demand.
Mentorship will take place through short-term, hands-on projects—such as building websites, designing fashion items, or installing solar systems—carried out under the supervision of mentors. These projects will lead to SkillBridge Micro-Certifications, and mentees will earn stipends, which will be funded through project revenue or through support from government, NGOs, and corporate sponsors.
After project completion, mentees will be guided toward two outcomes:
Employment with their mentors or other local businesses, or
Entrepreneurship, where they will be supported to start their own small-scale enterprises.
In the long term, SkillBridge will offer access to microgrants and connect promising entrepreneurs with angel investors, including members of the Nigerian diaspora who are committed to investing in youth and community development.
Rural Impact and Decentralization
SkillBridge will also launch a “Return-to-Rural” incentive program, encouraging trained mentors and mentees to establish new hubs in rural areas. This will help reduce rural-urban migration and stimulate job creation and innovation in underserved communities.
Revenue Model
To remain sustainable, SkillBridge will generate revenue through:
Mentor subscription plans for access to mentees and training resources.
Sponsorships from government agencies, NGOs, and corporate CSR programs.
Commissions from job placements or startup funding facilitation.
Premium workshops and educational content.
SkillBridge will not just train youths—it will transform them into creators of opportunity. By equipping Edo State’s young population with future-proof skills and connecting them to real economic pathways, SkillBridge will unlock a new era of inclusive growth and prosperity.

ideaSummary:
EduSpark Africa is an education technology and services company committed to transforming foundational education for children across Edo State, Nigeria. We focus on underserved communities where access to quality, future-relevant learning remains out of reach. Our mission is to bridge the gap between outdated classroom practices and the skills young learners need to succeed in a rapidly changing world.

In many parts of Nigeria, especially in low-income and rural areas, children are still taught using rigid, outdated curricula with little to no engagement or digital exposure. Teachers are undertrained and poorly equipped, resulting in weak learning outcomes, low enthusiasm among students, and a lack of practical, 21st-century skills. The result is a growing population of learners who are not only behind academically but also unprepared for life in a digital and entrepreneurial economy.

EduSpark Africa addresses these systemic challenges through three integrated, scalable solutions:
	1.	SparkClass Learning Kit (Offline + Online):
A low-cost, blended learning system combining printed workbooks or tablets with an offline-capable mobile app. It delivers gamified lessons in literacy, numeracy, and critical thinking, with animations, puzzles, and real-life career inspiration. Kits are distributed through schools, sold directly to parents, or subsidized through government or donor-supported programs.
	2.	EduSpark Micro Learning Hubs (Franchise Model):
These are 1–3 room afterschool and weekend centers located in rural communities and urban slums. Each hub is equipped with smart screens, a mini-library, and internet access. Trained local facilitators deliver micro-courses in coding, storytelling, public speaking, and creative problem-solving. This model empowers local youth to become franchise owners while offering families affordable, high-quality supplemental education in their own communities.
	3.	Curriculum Upgrade & Teacher Training Program:
EduSpark partners with schools—both public and private—to modernize lesson plans and teaching methods. We train teachers in blended learning, digital tools, and student-centered instruction. The program also embeds critical themes such as entrepreneurship, climate literacy, and civic responsibility into the curriculum to ensure children are not just literate, but equipped to lead and innovate.

Sustainable Impact:
EduSpark combines mission with market. Our model includes multiple revenue streams—from product sales and franchise fees to consulting contracts and digital subscriptions—ensuring long-term sustainability beyond grant cycles. Every naira invested amplifies our reach and impact, building a self-sustaining ecosystem of empowered learners, educators, and community entrepreneurs.

EduSpark Africa is not just improving education—it’s unlocking potential, transforming communities, and building a future where every child can thrive.

UC Impact Hub is a grassroots vocational and entrepreneurial training center based in Edo State, Nigeria, designed to combat the twin challenges of youth unemployment and education gaps. With over 60% of the population under 30, and widespread underemployment among graduates and school leavers, there is a growing need for practical, locally-relevant skill acquisition that leads directly to economic independence.

UC Impact Hub aims to bridge this divide by offering hands-on vocational skills training, digital literacy, and entrepreneurial support to youth from low-income or underserved communities. The center will initially train individuals in high-demand, low-barrier skill areas such as solar installation, tailoring, mobile phone repair, auto diagnostics, barbing, and social media marketing. Graduates will be linked with local businesses for internships or encouraged to launch small businesses of their own with access to mentorship, startup kits, and possibly a microloan program.

The hub's long-term vision includes becoming a self-sustaining, revenue-generating platform through affordable course fees, alumni partnerships, and CSR support from private sector actors. UC Impact Hub will also serve as a community rally point hosting guest speakers, youth-led innovation days, and mentorship events to foster ambition, confidence, and civic participation. It will not only equip youth with trades, but help them think critically, solve problems, and lead change in their neighborhoods.

ideaSummary:
PROMEBI KATFISH INDUSTRY is a fast-growing, registered agribusiness specializing in the processing and sales of hygienic, smoke-dried catfish. Founded in 2012 and officially registered in 2024, the business has been operating on a small scale from a home-based facility, currently processing and selling over 43200 kg of catfish monthly to customers across Nigeria and abroad. Our fish is carefully cleaned, preserved with food-grade salt, and sealed in branded packaging, earning a strong reputation for its freshness, crunchiness, and spiciness.

Driven by the rising demand for healthy, protein-rich, locally sourced fish, our goal is to expand operations into a fully mechanized and sustainable catfish processing facility. We plan to establish our own fish pond system on already secured land, acquire industrial-grade smoking kilns, sealing machines, digital measuring scales, and branded packaging materials. This upgrade will allow us to control the full value chain—from rearing to processing, packaging, and distribution—thereby increasing production, improving product quality, and boosting profitability.

The expansion will not only enhance our capacity but also create sustainable employment opportunities for 50 to 80+ individuals across multiple departments including farming, processing, logistics, sales, administration, and marketing. We also aim to provide industrial training opportunities for students in agriculture-related fields, empowering young people with practical skills and exposure to agribusiness.

With a ₦2 million grant, we will strategically allocate funds toward pond construction, equipment procurement, staff recruitment and training, branded packaging, marketing, and working capital. Our mission is to become a model for value-driven agribusiness in Nigeria by offering premium-quality catfish products while contributing to national goals of food security, youth employment, women empowerment, and economic diversification.

PROMEBI KATFISH INDUSTRY is built on strong values of quality, integrity, and impact. We are confident that with the right investment, we can scale our operations, enter new markets, and contribute meaningfully to socio-economic development—one fish at a time.
problemStatement:
PROMEBI KATFISH INDUSTRY is strategically positioned to solve several pressing economic, agricultural, and social challenges facing Nigeria today. These include unemployment, poor access to hygienically processed fish, weak value chains, overdependence on imported fish, and limited agro-processing capacity among small businesses.

Firstly, the business tackles the issue of unemployment and underemployment, particularly among youth and women. In Nigeria, many young people and women in rural and peri-urban areas lack access to sustainable income-generating opportunities. PROMEBI responds to this challenge by creating direct jobs for 50 to 80 individuals across the catfish farming and processing value chain. In addition, it offers hands-on training opportunities for students and young professionals in the fields of agriculture, food processing, and agribusiness, thereby empowering the next generation of agro-entrepreneurs.

Secondly, the business addresses the problem of poor access to clean, safe, and well-packaged processed fish. Consumers, especially in urban areas and the diaspora, often struggle to find quality, hygienically processed, and properly sealed catfish products. PROMEBI meets this need by producing smoke-dried catfish that is cleaned, salted with food-grade preservatives, and packaged in sealed, branded nylon to ensure freshness, taste, and hygiene. This not only improves the quality of food available to consumers but also enables the brand to meet both local and international market standards.

Another major challenge that PROMEBI solves is the heavy dependence on middlemen and unreliable supply chains. Many small-scale processors are disconnected from end consumers and struggle with inconsistent sales. PROMEBI mitigates this problem by controlling the entire value chain—from rearing to processing, packaging, and distribution—thereby reducing reliance on third parties. With plans to integrate digital marketing and e-commerce, the business ensures direct access to wholesalers, retailers, supermarkets, and final consumers.

PROMEBI also contributes significantly to improving food security and reducing the country’s dependence on imported fish. Despite Nigeria’s large agricultural base, the country continues to import a substantial amount of fish each year. By expanding local production through the establishment of a modern catfish pond and increasing processing capacity, PROMEBI enhances domestic supply, making high-protein food more accessible and affordable to the population.

In addition, the business addresses the limitations faced by many agro-entrepreneurs who lack the necessary tools and infrastructure to scale. By acquiring industrial smoking kilns, sealing machines, measuring scales, and branded packaging materials, PROMEBI is transforming its operations into a model for mechanized, large-scale fish processing. This transition not only boosts efficiency but also ensures quality control and standardization of products.

Furthermore, the business provides practical solutions to the shortage of experiential learning platforms for students in agriculture and food sciences. By creating a hub for industrial training, PROMEBI serves as a learning ground where students can gain real-world exposure, acquire market-relevant skills, and become better prepared for careers in agribusiness.

Lastly, PROMEBI solves the problem of poor branding and packaging that limits many local products from competing in formal retail and export markets. Through the use of professional packaging, quality labeling, and customer-centric branding, the business is creating a recognizable product that stands out both locally and internationally.

Through these interventions, PROMEBI KATFISH INDUSTRY is not only running a profitable business but also delivering tangible impact in areas of food security, youth and women empowerment, job creation, and local economic development.
